stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\sqrt[3]{27x^{4}y^{-2}}\cdot\left(9x^{2}y\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$, where $x>0$ and $y>0$?
stimulus: A printmaker models how evenly ink spreads across an etched plate using two positive quantities: $x$, the depth of the etched lines, and $y$, the pressure of the press.
explanation: Write each factor with fractional exponents, and apply the exponent to the coefficient as well as to the variables. $\sqrt[3]{27x^{4}y^{-2}}=3x^{4/3}y^{-2/3}$ and $\left(9x^{2}y\right)^{-1/2}=\tfrac{1}{3}x^{-1}y^{-1/2}$. When you multiply, the coefficients cancel ($3\cdot\tfrac13=1$) and you add the exponents: $x^{4/3-1}=x^{1/3}$ and $y^{-2/3-1/2}=y^{-7/6}$. Over a denominator of 6 this is $\dfrac{x^{2/6}}{y^{7/6}}=\sqrt[6]{\dfrac{x^{2}}{y^{7}}}$. Check with $x=2$, $y=3$: both the original and this choice come to about $0.350$.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. You took the cube root of the variables but left the 27 as it was, then multiplied it by $9^{-1/2}=\tfrac13$ and got 9. The cube root applies to 27 as well, which gives 3, so the coefficients cancel to 1.

B.why: You converted everything correctly but lost a sign when you combined the powers of $y$. You worked out $-\tfrac23+\tfrac12=-\tfrac16$, but the second exponent is $-\tfrac12$, so the sum is $-\tfrac23-\tfrac12=-\tfrac76$.

D.why: You multiplied the exponents of matching bases when you should have added them. For $x$ you did $\tfrac43\cdot(-1)=-\tfrac43$, and for $y$ you did $(-\tfrac23)(-\tfrac12)=\tfrac13$. When you multiply two powers of the same base, you add the exponents.

stem:
Which of the following expressions are equivalent to the given expression?

I. $\sqrt[12]{2^{n}}$
II. $\sqrt[24]{4^{n}}$
III. $\dfrac{\sqrt[4]{2^{n}}}{\sqrt[3]{2^{n}}}$
stimulus: A musicologist studying twelve-tone equal temperament writes the frequency ratio between two pitches that are $n$ semitones apart as $\dfrac{\left(\sqrt[4]{8}\right)^{n}}{\sqrt[3]{4^{n}}}$, where $n$ is a positive integer.
explanation: Rewrite everything as a power of 2. $\left(\sqrt[4]{8}\right)^{n}=\left(2^{3}\right)^{n/4}=2^{3n/4}$ and $\sqrt[3]{4^{n}}=\left(2^{2}\right)^{n/3}=2^{2n/3}$, so the ratio is $2^{3n/4-2n/3}=2^{n/12}$. I: $\sqrt[12]{2^{n}}=2^{n/12}$, so it is equivalent. II: $\sqrt[24]{4^{n}}=\left(2^{2}\right)^{n/24}=2^{n/12}$, so it is equivalent. III: $2^{n/4}\div2^{n/3}=2^{n/4-n/3}=2^{-n/12}$, which is the reciprocal and not equal for any positive $n$. So only I and II are equivalent.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. You confirmed statement I and stopped, or you rejected II because its base is 4 and you did not rewrite $4^{n}$ as $2^{2n}$. Once you do, II is $2^{2n/24}=2^{n/12}$, so it is also equivalent.

C.why: You rejected II because you did not rewrite base 4 as $2^{2}$. You also accepted III because you subtracted its exponents in the wrong order and got $\tfrac13-\tfrac14=\tfrac1{12}$. The quotient is $2^{n/4-n/3}$, which gives a negative exponent, so III is the reciprocal of the ratio.

D.why: You handled I and II correctly, but in III you subtracted the exponents in the wrong order. The numerator's exponent $\tfrac{n}{4}$ is smaller than the denominator's $\tfrac{n}{3}$, so III equals $2^{-n/12}$, not $2^{n/12}$.

stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{(8x^{2}y)^{2}}}{\sqrt{4xy^{-1}}}$, where $x>0$ and $y>0$?
stimulus: An immunologist compares two antibody-binding measurements, $x$ and $y$, using the given expression.
explanation: Write the numerator as $(8x^{2}y)^{2/3} = 8^{2/3}x^{4/3}y^{2/3} = 4x^{4/3}y^{2/3}$. Write the denominator as $(4xy^{-1})^{1/2} = 2x^{1/2}y^{-1/2}$. Now divide: the coefficient is $4 \div 2 = 2$, the power of $x$ is $\tfrac{4}{3}-\tfrac{1}{2}=\tfrac{5}{6}$, and the power of $y$ is $\tfrac{2}{3}-(-\tfrac{1}{2})=\tfrac{7}{6}$. That gives $2x^{5/6}y^{7/6}$.

A.why: You treated $y^{-1/2}$ in the denominator as if it were $y^{1/2}$ and worked out $\tfrac{2}{3}-\tfrac{1}{2}$. Subtracting a negative exponent adds it, so the power is $\tfrac{7}{6}$.

C.why: You took the square root of $x$ and $y^{-1}$ but not of the 4, so the coefficient became $4 \div 4 = 1$. The root applies to the coefficient too: $\sqrt{4}=2$.

D.why: You multiplied the numerator and denominator instead of dividing, so you added exponents ($\tfrac{4}{3}+\tfrac{1}{2}$) and multiplied the coefficients ($4 \cdot 2$).

stem:
Which of the following expressions are equivalent to $\dfrac{x^{1/2}}{\sqrt[4]{x^{5}}}$, where $x>0$?

I. $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt[3]{x^{4}}}$
II. $\dfrac{\sqrt[4]{x}}{x}$
III. $\sqrt{x^{-1}}\cdot\sqrt[4]{x^{-1}}$
stimulus: An ecologist's model of how a seed bank shrinks uses the given expression, where $x$ is the soil depth in centimeters.
explanation: The given expression is $x^{2/4-5/4}=x^{-3/4}$. Check each form on its own. I is $x^{-4/3}$, so it is not equivalent. II is $x^{1/4-1}=x^{-3/4}$, so it is equivalent. III is $x^{-1/2}\cdot x^{-1/4}=x^{-3/4}$, so it is equivalent. The answer is II and III only.

A.why: You confirmed II and stopped, or you rejected III without converting it. When you multiply the two roots, the exponents add: $-\tfrac{1}{2}+(-\tfrac{1}{4})=-\tfrac{3}{4}$.

B.why: You read $\sqrt[3]{x^{4}}$ as $x^{3/4}$ by flipping the index and the power. You also multiplied the exponents in III instead of adding them. The root index goes in the denominator: $\sqrt[3]{x^{4}}=x^{4/3}$.

D.why: You accepted I by reading $\sqrt[3]{x^{4}}$ as $x^{3/4}$. The index of the root is the denominator of the exponent, so I is $x^{-4/3}$.

A.why: You halved the exponent of $3^{2x-2}$ without changing the base. Halving the exponent is only allowed when you square the base at the same time, which turns 3 into 9.

B.why: You halved $2x$ but not the 4 when you took the square root, so you got $3^{x+4}$ and then $3^{2x-4}$. The root halves the whole exponent: $(2x+4)/2=x+2$.

C.why: You changed the base to 9 but kept the exponent $2x-2$. Squaring the base doubles every power, so you have to halve the exponent to make up for it.

stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{8a^{2}}{b}}\cdot\sqrt{\dfrac{b^{3}}{4a}}$, where $a>0$ and $b>0$?
stimulus: A materials scientist estimates how a composite panel stiffens using the given expression, where $a$ and $b$ are the thicknesses of its two layers.
explanation: The first factor is $2a^{2/3}b^{-1/3}$. The second is $\dfrac{b^{3/2}}{2a^{1/2}}$. Multiply them: the coefficients give $2 \div 2 = 1$, the power of $a$ is $\tfrac{2}{3}-\tfrac{1}{2}=\tfrac{1}{6}$, and the power of $b$ is $-\tfrac{1}{3}+\tfrac{3}{2}=\tfrac{7}{6}$. Since $a^{1/6}b^{7/6}=b\cdot a^{1/6}b^{1/6}$, the expression equals $b\sqrt[6]{ab}$.

B.why: You took the roots of the variables but left the coefficients alone, so you got $8 \div 4 = 2$. Taking the roots first gives $\sqrt[3]{8}=2$ and $\sqrt{4}=2$, which cancel.

C.why: You treated the $b$ in the denominator of the cube root as $b^{+1/3}$ and got $b^{11/6}$. Because $b$ is in the denominator, its exponent is $-\tfrac{1}{3}$.

D.why: You multiplied the radicands and added the indices $3+2$. You can't combine roots with different indices that way. Convert both to fractional exponents first.

stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\left(\dfrac{16p^{-4}q^{6}}{p^{2}q^{-2}}\right)^{-3/4}$, where $p>0$ and $q>0$?
stimulus: A public health analyst uses the given expression to adjust a vaccination-rate index, where $p$ and $q$ are positive population measures.
explanation: First simplify inside the parentheses: $16p^{-4-2}q^{6-(-2)}=16p^{-6}q^{8}$. Then raise each part to the $-\tfrac{3}{4}$ power. $16^{-3/4}=\tfrac{1}{8}$, $p^{(-6)(-3/4)}=p^{9/2}$, and $q^{8(-3/4)}=q^{-6}$. The result is $\dfrac{p^{9/2}}{8q^{6}}=\dfrac{p^{4}\sqrt{p}}{8q^{6}}$.

A.why: You applied the negative exponent to the variables but not to the coefficient, so you wrote $16^{3/4}=8$ in the numerator. The 16 is raised to $-\tfrac{3}{4}$ as well, which gives $\tfrac{1}{8}$.

C.why: You multiplied by the denominator instead of dividing, so you got $16p^{-2}q^{4}$ inside the parentheses. Dividing subtracts exponents: $-4-2=-6$ and $6-(-2)=8$.

D.why: You lost a sign on the $p$ term. A negative exponent times a negative exponent is positive: $(-6)(-\tfrac{3}{4})=\tfrac{9}{2}$, so $p$ belongs in the numerator.

stem:
Which of the following expressions are equivalent to $\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{x^{2}y}}{\sqrt[6]{xy^{5}}}$, where $x>0$ and $y>0$?

I. $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{y}}$
II. $\dfrac{\sqrt{xy}}{y}$
III. $\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{x}{y^{4}}}$
stimulus: An urban planner compares street density, $x$, with lot size, $y$, in two districts using the given expression.
explanation: The given expression is $x^{2/3-1/6}y^{1/3-5/6}=x^{1/2}y^{-1/2}$. I is $x^{1/2}y^{-1/2}$, so it is equivalent. II is $x^{1/2}y^{1/2-1}=x^{1/2}y^{-1/2}$, so it is equivalent. III is $x^{1/3}y^{-4/3}$, so it is not. The answer is I and II only.

A.why: You confirmed I and stopped. II is the same value with the denominator rationalized: $\dfrac{\sqrt{xy}}{y}=x^{1/2}y^{-1/2}$.

B.why: You divided the radicands even though the roots have different indices, and you rejected II. The indices must match before you can combine radicands, so convert to fractional exponents. II does pass that check.

D.why: You accepted III, which comes from dividing $x^{2}y$ by $xy^{5}$ under a single cube root. A cube root and a sixth root can't be combined like that.

stem: If $\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{a^{4}}\cdot a^{-1/2}}{\left(\sqrt{a}\right)^{-3}}=a^{k}$ for all positive values of $a$, what is the value of $k$?
stimulus: An archaeologist uses the given relationship to scale the estimated age of buried layers, where $a$ is the depth of a layer.

A.why: You subtracted $\tfrac{3}{2}$ for the denominator. The denominator's exponent is $-\tfrac{3}{2}$, and subtracting a negative means adding.

B.why: You wrote $\sqrt[3]{a^{4}}$ as $a^{3/4}$. The power goes on top and the index goes on the bottom, so it is $a^{4/3}$.

D.why: You added the exponents in $(a^{1/2})^{-3}$ and got $-\tfrac{5}{2}$. When you raise a power to a power, you multiply the exponents: $\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot(-3)=-\tfrac{3}{2}$.

stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\dfrac{\sqrt{9w\sqrt[3]{w^{2}}}}{w^{-1/6}}$, where $w>0$?
stimulus: An ornithologist uses the given expression to model how wing loading changes with body mass $w$, in grams, for a species of warbler.
explanation: Inside the square root, $w\cdot w^{2/3}=w^{5/3}$. Taking the square root of $9w^{5/3}$ gives $3w^{5/6}$. Dividing by $w^{-1/6}$ adds $\tfrac{1}{6}$ to the exponent: $3w^{5/6+1/6}=3w$.

B.why: You took the square root of the variable part but not the 9. The outer root covers everything under it, so $\sqrt{9}=3$.

C.why: You subtracted $\tfrac{1}{6}$ when dividing by $w^{-1/6}$. Dividing by a negative power adds its size: $\tfrac{5}{6}+\tfrac{1}{6}=1$.

D.why: You multiplied $w\cdot w^{2/3}$ by multiplying the exponents and got $w^{2/3}$. When you multiply powers of the same base, you add the exponents, which gives $w^{5/3}$.
